question: Which part of the cell acts as the main control center and holds the genetic material?
explanation: The nucleus holds the DNA and directs all the activities of the cell. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is the outer membrane of a cell described as selectively permeable?

options.A: It completely blocks all water from crossing
options.B: It controls which substances enter and leave the cell
options.C: It generates energy for internal transport
options.D: It provides a rigid wall for structural support

explanation: Selective permeability means the membrane allows certain molecules to pass through while keeping others out to maintain balance inside the cell. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which part of the cell is mainly responsible for producing energy?
explanation: Mitochondria convert nutrients into usable energy for the cell. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which of the following structures does not have its own surrounding membrane?
explanation: Ribosomes are simple structures made of RNA and protein that build proteins for the cell. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h2)

question: During which phase of the cell cycle does the cell copy its DNA?
explanation: The cell spends most of its life in interphase, growing and duplicating its DNA to prepare for division. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the main reason a cell copies its DNA before dividing?

options.A: To clear out damaged proteins from the fluid cytoplasm
options.B: To ensure each new cell receives an identical set of instructions
options.C: To provide extra energy molecules for splitting
options.D: To repair the outer membrane against stress

explanation: Copying DNA guarantees that daughter cells inherit the exact genetic blueprint needed to function properly. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h3)

question: What happens to the chromosomes during the metaphase stage of cell division?

options.A: They copy their genetic material twice
options.B: They pack tightly inside the nucleus
options.C: They line up along the middle of the cell
options.D: They pull apart toward opposite ends

explanation: During metaphase, chromosomes line up in the center to make sure they separate evenly. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h4)

question: A skin scrape heals over several days as new cells form. Which process drives this healing?
explanation: Body tissue repair relies on mitotic division to produce identical replacement cells. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h4)

question: How many chromosomes are found in a normal human egg or sperm cell?
explanation: Sex cells have 23 chromosomes, which is half the normal body cell count of 46. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is crossing over during meiosis important?

options.A: It stops mutations from happening in sex cells
options.B: It speeds up how fast normal cells divide
options.C: It doubles the total amount of cellular DNA
options.D: It creates genetic variety among offspring

explanation: Crossing over mixes genes from parents, making every sperm and egg cell unique. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main cause of uncontrolled tissue growth or tumor formation?

options.A: An increase in energy production by mitochondria
options.B: Normal completion of cell division in body tissues
options.C: Eating too much protein during pregnancy
options.D: Failure of the cell cycle control system

explanation: Tumors form when cells ignore normal stopping signals and continue to divide without control. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is a routine cervical screening test recommended during reproductive health checkups?

options.A: To detect early cell changes before cancer develops
options.B: To check energy levels in body tissues
options.C: To measure the exact number of chromosomes in the blood
options.D: To confirm whether fertilization has happened

explanation: Screening tests identify unusual cell changes early so treatment can prevent cancer from developing. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T2#BMP111_U1_T2_h6)
